summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging after a release PR merge, then investigate and fix slow IPNS publish times and broken token refresh discovered during smoke testing.
summary.outcome: Successfully unblocked staging deployment via manual v0.25.1 tag after fixing a release-please config bug; submitted PRs for fire-and-forget IPNS publish optimization (#308) and a major API client consolidation refactor (#309) that eliminated 8800 lines of generated code and unified token refresh into a single interceptor.

repo: The staging deployment workflow triggers on `v*-staging*` tags only — release tags do not auto-deploy to staging. A manual 'Tag Staging Release' GitHub Actions workflow exists to run E2E tests, get approval, create the staging tag, and trigger deploy.

release-please aborts tag creation if merged release PRs have a `pull-request-title-pattern` without `${component}` — it can't match the PR back to its components and considers releases 'untagged', blocking future releases.

The web app had three separate HTTP client paths: orval React Query hooks (fetch-based custom-instance.ts), a hand-written axios client (lib/api/client.ts), and bare IPFS functions. Token refresh only existed on the axios client.

The web app's orval React Query generation produced 8,812 lines of hooks but only 1 hook (useHealthControllerCheck) was actually used — all other callers imported the raw generated functions, identical to what @cipherbox/api-client already provides.

The API is a zero-knowledge server that never handles plaintext — it stores opaque blobs, manages auth, and proxies IPFS. This is why @cipherbox/api-client (shared types/crypto) is correctly absent from API dependencies.
The @cipherbox/api-client package uses axios-functions orval mode for framework-agnostic consumers; the web app previously had a separate react-query orval generation from the same OpenAPI spec.
CI had a verify step checking apps/web/src/api/ for generated code drift — this needed updating after the consolidation removed that directory.
The Grafana Cloud free-tier hibernates after inactivity and returns HTTP 503 'instance is loading' on first wake — transient, not a real deployment failure.

The apps/api Dockerfile had a stale COPY for packages/crypto/package.json even though @cipherbox/api never imports any workspace packages — this caused pnpm deploy to fail when @cipherbox/crypto added @cipherbox/core as a devDependency.

code.finding: IPNS publishRecord() was awaiting delegated routing DHT publish via someguy sidecar, causing 10-30s delays. Changed to fire-and-forget since resolveRecord() always prefers DB cache. Added trailing .catch() to prevent unhandled rejection on metrics observe() failure.

Stale COPY for packages/crypto/package.json was present even though @cipherbox/api has no workspace dependencies. Removing it fixes pnpm deploy failures when transitive devDependencies of crypto pull in additional workspace packages.

Extended ApiClientConfig to support refreshAccessToken callback, onRefreshFailure callback, and withCredentials flag. Added 401 response interceptor with shared-promise deduplication to prevent concurrent refresh races.
Had unsafe `as` type casts (e.g. `as { token: string }`) bypassing generated DTO types. Fixed by using generated DTOs directly from @cipherbox/api-client models.

Progress download path used raw fetch() bypassing the API client interceptor (no 401 refresh). Consolidated to use axios with onDownloadProgress — the comment claiming axios byte counts are unreliable was incorrect for blob responses.

pull-request-title-pattern was set to 'chore: release' without ${component}. With multi-package config, release-please cannot match merged PRs back to components, causing it to abort with 'untagged, merged release PRs outstanding'.

workflow: When release-please is stuck due to unmatched component PRs, the unblock path is: fix the config on a new branch AND manually create the tag+release via `git tag` + `gh release create` from the correct commit.
chore commits do not trigger release-please version bumps — only feat and fix do. Use fix(ci) for broken build fixes to get a patch release.
CodeRabbit and GitHub Copilot both flagged the same unhandled promise rejection issue independently — worth checking both review sources before resolving.
Codecov patch coverage checks will fail on fire-and-forget error paths (catch handlers) that aren't exercised by existing tests — need explicit tests for error branches even when they're defensive.

friction: release-please silently aborted v0.25.1 tag creation with a non-obvious error about 'untagged merged release PRs' — required digging through workflow logs to find the root cause.

v0.25.0 staging deployment was blocked until v0.25.1 was manually tagged because the Tag Staging Release workflow checks out the release tag commit, so the Dockerfile fix had to be included in a new release.

The web app had accumulated three separate HTTP client paths with inconsistent auth handling — token refresh was only wired to one of them, which was only discovered via a long-running smoke test triggering a 401.
The Dockerfile build failure error message ('pnpm deploy can't find @cipherbox/core') required tracing through workspace dependencies to understand the stale COPY was the cause.
Grafana provisioning step caused a false alarm in the staging deployment workflow due to free-tier hibernation.
open_items: PR #309 (API client consolidation) needs CI to pass after the verify step was updated to remove apps/web/src/api/ references.
PR #308 (IPNS fire-and-forget) and PR #309 (API consolidation) both need to be merged before Tag Staging Release can be run with a clean v0.25.1+ tag.

The token refresh fix from the initial debugger investigation (shared token-refresh.ts) was stashed/superseded by the full API client consolidation refactor — verify the consolidated approach fully covers all refresh scenarios the debugger identified.
PR #307 (release-please title pattern fix) needs to be merged to prevent the same 'untagged release PR' abort from happening on future releases.
IPNS publish performance should be validated on staging after v0.25.1+ deploys — the fire-and-forget fix should bring publish time from 30s+ down to near-instant.
